title: Truncation adjunctions and right orthogonality for fixed pairs
statement:
Let $\mathcal T$ be a triangulated category with a t-structure $t=(\mathcal T^{\le0},\mathcal T^{\ge0})$ [def-weil-t-structure], and let $\Phi:\mathcal T\to\mathcal T$ be an exact triangulated autoequivalence which, together with its inverse, preserves both t-structure classes. Let $\mathcal T^\Phi$ be the category of fixed pairs [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category]: an object is $(X,\theta)$ with $\theta:\Phi X\xrightarrow{\sim}X$, and morphisms $f$ satisfy $f\theta_X=\theta_Y\Phi(f)$.

For each integer $n$, the canonical truncation functors $\tau^{\le n},\tau^{\ge n}$ lift to functors on $\mathcal T^\Phi$. Their underlying objects and morphisms are the usual truncations, and the canonical truncation maps are morphisms of fixed pairs. On fixed pairs with underlying objects in $\mathcal T^{\le n}$, respectively $\mathcal T^{\ge n}$, the usual right, respectively left, truncation adjunctions hold. In particular, for every fixed pair $(X,\theta)$,
$$
 X\in\mathcal T^{\ge0}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T^\Phi}\bigl((M,\theta_M),(X,\theta)\bigr)=0
 \quad\text{for every fixed pair with }M\in\mathcal T^{\le-1}.
$$
No triangulated structure on $\mathcal T^\Phi$ is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3 and 1.3.4, printed pp. 29–30; fixed-pair consequence of uniqueness and naturality, made explicit here

proof.text: Fix an integer $n$. Since $\Phi$ is exact it commutes with $[1]$ up to natural isomorphism, and $\mathcal T^{\le n}=\mathcal T^{\le0}[-n]$, $\mathcal T^{\ge n}=\mathcal T^{\ge0}[-n]$ are strictly full [def-weil-t-structure]; hence $\Phi$ preserves $\mathcal T^{\le n}$ and $\mathcal T^{\ge n+1}$ for every $n$. For $X\in\mathcal T$ take the truncation triangle $\tau^{\le n}X\xrightarrow{\iota_X}X\xrightarrow{\pi_X}\tau^{\ge n+1}X\to$ of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles], clause 1. Applying $\Phi$ gives a distinguished triangle $\Phi\tau^{\le n}X\to\Phi X\to\Phi\tau^{\ge n+1}X\to$ with outer terms in $\mathcal T^{\le n}$ and $\mathcal T^{\ge n+1}$, so by the uniqueness up to unique isomorphism in that clause there are unique isomorphisms $c_X:\Phi\tau^{\le n}X\xrightarrow{\sim}\tau^{\le n}\Phi X$, $d_X:\Phi\tau^{\ge n+1}X\xrightarrow{\sim}\tau^{\ge n+1}\Phi X$ with $\iota_{\Phi X}c_X=\Phi(\iota_X)$ and $d_X\Phi(\pi_X)=\pi_{\Phi X}$. For $f:X\to Y$, both $c_Y\Phi(\tau^{\le n}f)$ and $\tau^{\le n}(\Phi f)c_X$ are maps $\Phi\tau^{\le n}X\to\tau^{\le n}\Phi Y$ whose composite with $\iota_{\Phi Y}$ is $\Phi(f\iota_X)$; by the right adjunction of the same clause (source in $\mathcal T^{\le n}$) they agree, so $c$ is natural; dually $d$ is natural. For a fixed pair $(X,\theta)$ put $\theta^{\le n}=\tau^{\le n}(\theta)\circ c_X:\Phi\tau^{\le n}X\xrightarrow{\sim}\tau^{\le n}X$ and $\theta^{\ge n+1}=\tau^{\ge n+1}(\theta)\circ d_X$. Then $\iota_X\theta^{\le n}=\iota_X\tau^{\le n}(\theta)c_X=\theta\,\iota_{\Phi X}c_X=\theta\,\Phi(\iota_X)$, so $\iota_X$ is a morphism of fixed pairs [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category]; dually for $\pi_X$. If $f:(X,\theta)\to(Y,\theta')$ is a morphism of fixed pairs, then $\tau^{\le n}(f)\theta^{\le n}=\tau^{\le n}(f\theta)c_X=\tau^{\le n}(\theta'\Phi f)c_X=\tau^{\le n}(\theta')c_Y\Phi(\tau^{\le n}f)=\theta'^{\le n}\Phi(\tau^{\le n}f)$ by naturality of $c$, and dually for $\tau^{\ge n+1}$. Identities and composites are those of $\mathcal T$, so these assignments are functors on $\mathcal T^\Phi$ lifting $\tau^{\le n},\tau^{\ge n+1}$ (every $\tau^{\ge m}$ is some $\tau^{\ge n+1}$).

source.place: Propositions 1.3.3–1.3.4; uniqueness and functoriality of truncation triangles

proof.text: Let $(M,\theta_M)$ be a fixed pair with $M\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$ and $(X,\theta)$ any fixed pair. By the right adjunction of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles], clause 1, $h\mapsto\iota_Xh$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(M,\tau^{\le n}X)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(M,X)$. If $h$ is equivariant so is $\iota_Xh$, a composite of morphisms of fixed pairs (step 1, [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category]). Conversely let $g=\iota_Xh$ be equivariant. The two maps $h\theta_M$ and $\theta^{\le n}\Phi(h)$ from $\Phi M$ to $\tau^{\le n}X$ satisfy $\iota_Xh\theta_M=g\theta_M=\theta\Phi(g)$ and $\iota_X\theta^{\le n}\Phi(h)=\theta\Phi(\iota_X)\Phi(h)=\theta\Phi(g)$; since $\Phi M\in\mathcal T^{\le n}$ (step 1), injectivity of the same adjunction bijection for the source $\Phi M$ gives $h\theta_M=\theta^{\le n}\Phi(h)$, so $h$ is equivariant. Thus the bijection restricts to $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T^\Phi}(M,\tau^{\le n}X)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T^\Phi}(M,X)$. Dually, for a fixed pair $M$ with $M\in\mathcal T^{\ge n+1}$, $h\mapsto h\pi_X$ restricts the left adjunction bijection to $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T^\Phi}(\tau^{\ge n+1}X,M)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T^\Phi}(X,M)$: if $g=h\pi_X$ is equivariant, the two maps $h\theta^{\ge n+1}$ and $\theta_M\Phi(h)$ from $\Phi\tau^{\ge n+1}X$ to $M$ both give $g\theta=\theta_M\Phi(g)$ after precomposition with $\Phi(\pi_X)=d_X^{-1}\pi_{\Phi X}$ (for the first, $h\tau^{\ge n+1}(\theta)d_X\Phi(\pi_X)=h\tau^{\ge n+1}(\theta)\pi_{\Phi X}=h\pi_X\theta$); since $M\in\mathcal T^{\ge n+1}$, injectivity of the left adjunction bijection for $\Phi X$, transported along $d_X$, makes them equal, so $h$ is equivariant.

source.place: Proposition 1.3.3; truncation adjunctions, with the fixed-pair naturality consequence made explicit

proof.text: Suppose first $X\in\mathcal T^{\ge0}$ and let $(M,\theta_M)$ be a fixed pair with $M\in\mathcal T^{\le-1}$. Write $M=A[1]$ with $A\in\mathcal T^{\le0}$; then $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(M,X)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(A,X[-1])=0$ by axiom 2 of [def-weil-t-structure]. So the underlying morphism of any equivariant $M\to X$ is zero, and the morphism is zero since the forgetful functor of [def-weil-endofunctor-fixed-pair-category] is faithful (its zero morphism is the underlying zero map). Conversely assume every equivariant map from such a fixed pair to $(X,\theta)$ is zero. By step 1 with $n=-1$, $(A,\theta^{\le-1})=(\tau^{\le-1}X,\theta^{\le-1})$ is a fixed pair with $A\in\mathcal T^{\le-1}$ and $\iota_X:A\to X$ is equivariant, so $\iota_X=0$. Under the bijection of step 2, $\operatorname{id}_A\in\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T^\Phi}(A,A)$ maps to $\iota_X=0$, as does $0$; injectivity gives $\operatorname{id}_A=0$, so $A$ is a zero object. In the distinguished truncation triangle $A\to X\xrightarrow{\pi_X}\tau^{\ge0}X\to A[1]$ of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles], clause 1, the two terms $A$, $A[1]$ are zero, so $\pi_X$ is an isomorphism (long exact Hom sequence; elementary). As $\tau^{\ge0}X\in\mathcal T^{\ge0}$ and the class is strictly full, $X\in\mathcal T^{\ge0}$. This is BBD 1.3.4 ((a)$\Leftrightarrow$(b)) with Hom taken in $\mathcal T^\Phi$. Edge cases: $X=0$ satisfies both sides; for $X\in\mathcal T^{\le-1}$ nonzero, $(X,\theta)$ itself is a test pair with $\operatorname{id}\neq0$, matching $X\notin\mathcal T^{\ge0}$.

lean.statement: theorem fixedPairTruncationOrthogonality {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Preadditive C] [HasZeroObject C] [HasShift C ℤ] [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor C n).Additive] [Pretriangulated C] (t : Triangulated.TStructure C) (E : C ≌ C) [E.functor.CommShift ℤ] [E.functor.IsTriangulated] [E.inverse.CommShift ℤ] [E.inverse.IsTriangulated] (hle : ∀ (n : ℤ) (X : C), t.le n X → t.le n (E.functor.obj X)) (hge : ∀ (n : ℤ) (X : C), t.ge n X → t.ge n (E.functor.obj X)) (hleInv : ∀ (n : ℤ) (X : C), t.le n X → t.le n (E.inverse.obj X)) (hgeInv : ∀ (n : ℤ) (X : C), t.ge n X → t.ge n (E.inverse.obj X)) : (∀ (n : ℤ), ∃ (leTrunc geTrunc : ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (fun A : Endofunctor.Algebra E.functor => IsIso A.str) ⥤ ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (fun A : Endofunctor.Algebra E.functor => IsIso A.str)), ∃ (ι : leTrunc ⟶ 𝟭 _) (π : 𝟭 _ ⟶ geTrunc), (∀ (X : ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (fun A : Endofunctor.Algebra E.functor => IsIso A.str)), (leTrunc.obj X).obj.a = (t.truncLE n).obj X.obj.a ∧ (geTrunc.obj X).obj.a = (t.truncGE n).obj X.obj.a ∧ HEq (ι.app X).hom.f ((t.truncLEι n).app X.obj.a) ∧ HEq (π.app X).hom.f ((t.truncGEπ n).app X.obj.a)) ∧ (∀ (M X : ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (fun A : Endofunctor.Algebra E.functor => IsIso A.str)), t.le n M.obj.a → Function.Bijective (fun h : M ⟶ leTrunc.obj X => h ≫ ι.app X)) ∧ (∀ (X M : ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (fun A : Endofunctor.Algebra E.functor => IsIso A.str)), t.ge n M.obj.a → Function.Bijective (fun h : geTrunc.obj X ⟶ M => π.app X ≫ h))) ∧ (∀ (X : ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (fun A : Endofunctor.Algebra E.functor => IsIso A.str)), t.ge 0 X.obj.a ↔ ∀ (M : ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (fun A : Endofunctor.Algebra E.functor => IsIso A.str)), t.le (-1 : ℤ) M.obj.a → ∀ f : M ⟶ X, f.hom.f = 0)
